title: bug: Bind idle-launched CLI claims to task preflight and postflight
description:
A Codex CLI launched with 'Pre-flight Complete: no claimable task' is instructed to wait and claim inside the CLI, but scripts/moe-agent.ps1:4176 captures a baseline only for preflightOk + preflightTaskId and :5015 lands only preflightTaskId. Fresh in-CLI claims therefore have no task-bound wrapper delivery tracking (reproduced by worker-104791d9 and worker-6dd2f337 on 2026-09-11; both stopped before edits).
Keep waiting/claiming in the wrapper until a task-bound session can launch, or establish an equivalently verified pre-edit adoption boundary. Preserve task attribution, peer WIP, and crash recovery; no hand-created baseline or whole-tree staging.
definitionOfDone: Regression reproduces the no-task preflight -> in-CLI claim path and proves task-specific baseline exists before code edits and correct task postflight is not skipped.
Fix the supported launcher paths consistently without weakening recovery, attribution, or preserving unrelated peer work.
Fresh wrapper-launched canary demonstrates correct task binding and recorded path-specific landing; tests cover the idle and resume paths.
taskRails: Wrapper remains the only git actor; do not compensate with agent-side manual baselines or commits.
Preserve live peer ownership and dirty paths; do not relax attribution to bypass the missing boundary.

implementationPlan.description: RE-MEASURE ALL FOUR SITES - THE WRAPPERS MOVED SINCE THIS PLAN WAS FIRST WRITTEN. Read-only, no edits. task-e5a45262 (the QA recovery race) has LANDED since, and it edited these same two launchers plus both postflight harnesses, so every line number below is a starting point to verify, not a fact. In scripts/moe-agent.ps1: the taskless prompt block beginning '# Pre-flight Complete: no claimable task' tells the CLI to call wait_for_task, then claim, then get_context - so the claim happens INSIDE the CLI; the baseline block immediately after it is guarded on AutoClaim and preflightOk and preflightTaskId, so no baseline is taken; and the post-flight block formerly near line 5012 is guarded on AutoClaim and preflightTaskId, so no landing runs. In scripts/moe-agent.sh the same three sites were the taskless prompt near 5015, the pre-flight landing guard near 5098 and the session-ended guard near 1893. Net effect unchanged: a session that claims in-CLI edits code with no baseline and lands nothing, silently - the reproduction two workers hit on 2026-09-11. (b) READ WHAT THE SIBLING ADDED, because it changes this fix for the better: e5a45262 writes a live-session marker in the SAME pre-flight block that takes the baseline, and gates the recovery on probing that marker's process. Once this task moves the wait and the claim back into the wrapper, a claiming session flows through that block and therefore gets BOTH the baseline and the marker for free, with no new code here. Confirm that by reading the block rather than assuming it, and note in the step note that a chat-only session must get NEITHER - it holds no task, so there is nothing to key a marker or a baseline on. (c) Read scripts/tests/taskless-handoff.test.mjs completely before touching the wrappers. It renders the REAL taskless prompt blocks by slicing between literal marker comments - in PowerShell between the dynamicContext initialisation and the '# -------- Pre-flight baseline' comment, in bash between DYNAMIC_CONTEXT and the '# -------- Pre-flight landing: recovery' comment. Those comments are load-bearing: reword one and the harness stops finding its boundaries. It already runs in CI beside agent-runtime.test.mjs, so it is the regression home and no new test file is needed. (d) Read scripts/tests/parity-check.sh: it extracts the MOE_COMMIT_, MOE_ATTR_, MOE_CHECKPOINT_ and MOE_ATTRIBUTION_ families from both wrappers and fails on any asymmetry, so naming the new refusal inside MOE_COMMIT_REFUSED_ gets cross-wrapper enforcement free and needs no harness edit. (e) This task is epic-final, so its landing runs the full quality gate; keep the diff tight.
implementationPlan.note:
RE-MEASURED. Read-only, no edits. Line numbers in the plan are all stale; the wrappers moved twice, not once.

(a) FOUR SITES, CURRENT COORDINATES
ps1 (5431 lines): claim RPC 3988 (governor synthesises {hasNext:false} 3987); PREFLIGHT_NO_TASK set 4130-4131; taskless prompt branches 4344-4369; baseline block 4371-4406 guarded `$AutoClaim -and $preflightOk -and $preflightTaskId`; post-flight guard 5218 `$AutoClaim -and $preflightTaskId`; loop tail `} while ($loopEnabled)` 5384.
sh (6390 lines): claim RPC 4572; PREFLIGHT_NO_TASK 4864; NOTIFICATION_PROMPT 5148-5150; taskless DYNAMIC_CONTEXT 5258-5263; PROMPT_BODY taskless 5314-5315; fallback 5318; pre-flight landing 5337; per-CLI no-task fast paths 5684 (grok) + 5987 (claude); loop tail 6390.

(b) THE PLAN'S PREMISE IS PARTLY OBSOLETE - a SECOND sibling landed here: ea61fcb "fix(agent): return taskless notices to wrapper". It added (1) the $notificationPrompt / NOTIFICATION_PROMPT chat-only prompt, and (2) scripts/tests/taskless-handoff.test.mjs itself. So a taskless chat-only prompt ALREADY exists - but only for `claude` + non-interactive + loopEnabled + AutoClaim + non-governor. Separately, a no-task FAST PATH already skips the CLI launch entirely (ps1 4974, sh 5684/5987) when there are no routed mentions.

Net: the "wait+claim inside the CLI" hole is NARROWER than the card describes, but still real on four paths:
  H1  -NoLoop / -PollInterval 0: fast path is gated on $loopEnabled, so a single-shot taskless run DOES launch an editing CLI with "FIRST action MUST be moe.wait_for_task ... then claim_next_task".
  H2  routed mentions present + (interactive OR cli != claude): notification gate excludes them, so they get the claim-inviting prompt.
  H3  sh only: codex/gemini have NO fast path at all (grok+claude do), so those seats launch taskless on every poll. ps1's fast path is CLI-agnostic. Pre-existing sh/ps1 asymmetry that parity-check cannot see (it compares strings, not control flow).
  H4  claim RPC returns null (daemon/proxy down): both wrappers print "falling back to in-agent claim" and render the chat_channels->claim_next_task fallback body. Unbound editing CLI, same defect, different trigger. Step 6 names this explicitly.

(c) SIBLING e5a45262 CONFIRMED BY READING, NOT ASSUMED: the live-session marker is written by Invoke-MoePreflightBaseline inside the SAME baseline block (ps1 4371-4406) - so once the wrapper claims before launching, a claiming session gets baseline AND marker with zero new code here. A chat-only session correctly gets NEITHER: it holds no task, so there is nothing to key either file on. Post-flight Remove-MoeLiveMarker 5377 + outer finally 5403 are the removal sites; do not disturb.

(d) HARNESS BOUNDARIES VERIFIED (scripts/tests/taskless-handoff.test.mjs, 107 lines, 3 engines x 11 cases on win32):
  ps1 context slice  `    $dynamicContext = ""` (4196) -> `    # -------- Pre-flight baseline` (4371)
  ps1 body slice     `    $claimPromptBody = $null` (4494) -> `    $script:CliLaunchedAt = Get-Date` (4554)
  sh slice           `    DYNAMIC_CONTEXT=""` (5144) -> `    # -------- Pre-flight landing: recovery` (5337)
All four marker strings exist exactly once at those offsets. Every edit I make to the prompt branches is inside these slices; the wrapper-side wait is outside them (preflight), so step 2 must assert the wait on SOURCE text, not on rendered prompt.

CONFLICT I AM FLAGGING NOW (affects step 2's "leave every existing case untouched"): four existing cases encode the behaviour this task removes - `interactive`, `no-loop`, `other CLI` assert /FIRST action MUST be moe.wait_for_task/ and `preflight failure` asserts /moe.claim_next_task/ with auto:true. They are H1/H2/H4 written down as a contract. They must be rewritten, not preserved. `governor`, `claimed`, `resume` and `manual launch` (AutoClaim=false, operator opted out of baseline+landing entirely) stay untouched.

(e) MECHANISM CONFIRMED FOR STEP 3/4, no guesses:
  - moe.wait_for_task (packages/moe-daemon/src/tools/waitForTask.ts:209) takes {statuses, workerId, epicId?, timeoutMs?} (default 300000, max 600000) and returns hasNext+task / hasChatMessage+chatMessage / hasPendingQuestion / timedOut. It wakes on NEW MESSAGE_CREATED events only - it does NOT see already-unread mentions, so the wrapper must not enter the wait while unread mentions are pending or a reply is delayed by the whole timeout.
  - moe-proxy already tiers wait_for_task to WAIT_FOR_TASK_TIMEOUT_MS = 11 min (packages/moe-proxy/src/index.ts:36) vs the 30s default, so the existing Invoke-MoeRpc / moe_rpc helper can carry it unchanged. No new RPC plumbing.
  - moe.list_workers returns currentTaskId per worker (tools/listWorkers.ts:48) and is side-effect-free: that is the adoption probe for step 4. claim_next_task must NOT be used there - it would claim.
  - parity-check.sh extracts \b(MOE_COMMIT_|MOE_ATTR_|MOE_CHECKPOINT_|MOE_ATTRIBUTION_)[A-Z0-9_]*\b from both files and diffs the sets, so naming the refusal MOE_COMM

implementationPlan.description: RED FIRST, IN THE EXISTING HARNESS. Add cases to scripts/tests/taskless-handoff.test.mjs, leaving every existing case untouched - including any the recovery-race sibling added. They must fail against the current wrappers, which is what the epic rail requires. Assert on the rendered taskless block and on the guard expressions rather than on a transcription of them: the taskless prompt must no longer instruct the CLI to claim a task, since a session that may edit code is only ever launched with a task already bound, and the guard deciding whether a baseline is taken must no longer be the sole gate that silently skips the whole delivery path when no task was claimed at pre-flight. Add the chat-only case explicitly: when the wrapper wakes for a routed mention rather than a task, the prompt it renders must tell that session to answer the mention and NOT to claim or edit, because it has no baseline by design. Add the adoption case: a session that began with no task but ends holding one must produce the named refusal rather than silence. Cover BOTH wrappers for every case - the harness already renders both, and a fix landing in only one is the failure mode this repository has hit before. Run `node --test scripts/tests/taskless-handoff.test.mjs` and save the red output. It must be an assertion failure about rendered content; a boundary-slicing error means you moved a marker comment and must put it back.
implementationPlan.note:
RED FIRST, captured before any wrapper edit.

`node --test scripts/tests/taskless-handoff.test.mjs` against the UNCHANGED wrappers: tests 39, pass 21, fail 18. Every pre-existing case stayed green (the 9 taskless-headless role cases x 3 engines, governor, claimed, resume, manual launch); only the new/changed ones failed, and they failed on RENDERED CONTENT, never on a boundary slice - the four marker comments the harness slices on are untouched and I verified their offsets in step 1.

What I added to scripts/tests/taskless-handoff.test.mjs
- New fixture knob `claimFailed` -> `$preflightClaimFailed` / `PREFLIGHT_CLAIM_FAILED`, so the claim-RPC-failure shape can be rendered instead of inferred.
- Four cases asserting a taskless launch a CLAIMING role can reach under AutoClaim is chat-only and never claims: `interactive`, `no-loop`, `other CLI` (codex), `claim RPC failure`. Each asserts on BOTH rendered parts (dynamic context AND prompt body) that the prompt says notification-only, still routes moe.chat_send, forbids claiming, forbids editing - and that neither the "FIRST action MUST be moe.wait_for_task" chain nor the "when it returns hasNext:true" chain survives anywhere.
- Three guard cases per wrapper (six total), on SOURCE text because the wait and the post-flight live outside the rendered slices: the wrapper calls wait_for_task through its own RPC helper (ps1 `Invoke-MoeRpc -Tool "wait_for_task"`, sh `moe_rpc wait_for_task` - neither can be satisfied by prompt text); all three named taskless outcomes exist (`MOE_TASKLESS_NO_LAUNCH reason=idle|wait-failed|claim-failed`); and `MOE_COMMIT_REFUSED_ADOPTED_NO_BASELINE` exists.
- Preserved untouched: governor, claimed, resume, manual launch (AutoClaim=false - the operator opting out of wrapper claiming, baseline and landing, where the in-CLI chain is still correct).

DEVIATION FROM THE STEP TEXT, flagged deliberately. The step said to leave every existing case untouched. Four of them (`interactive`, `no-loop`, `other CLI`, `preflight failure`) were the defect written down as a contract - they asserted the claim-inviting prompt on exactly the paths this task closes. Preserving them would have made the fix untestable. They are rewritten, not deleted; coverage went up, not down. I also dropped one case I had briefly added (`manual claim failure`, auto:false + claimFailed): AutoClaim=false renders no PROMPT_BODY at all, so the fixture asserted a shape that cannot exist.

BEHAVIOURAL COVERAGE, because the prompt harness only renders strings. A grep-for-a-new-code assertion fails on old code trivially and proves nothing about behaviour (mem:pattern-postflight-red-proof-via-temp-tree), so the two real cases went into the harness that actually runs the wrapper end-to-end:
- scripts/tests/postflight.sh + postflight.ps1 scenario AA "a taskless single-shot run never launches an unbound CLI": FAKE_CLAIM_MODE=idle, --no-loop (the exact shape whose fast path was gated off by loopEnabled). Asserts the fake CLI's file was NEVER created and that the suppression is named. On the old wrappers a CLI DOES launch here - observed directly, see below.
- scenario AB "a chat-only session that adopts a task refuses to land, loudly": wait wakes on a chat message, the chat-only CLI writes a file, the worker turns out to hold task-adopted. Asserts MOE_COMMIT_REFUSED_ADOPTED_NO_BASELINE task=task-adopted, HEAD unmoved, the session's own bytes still untracked, a PEER's dirty file untouched, and the #governors line actually written to the message store. implementationPlan.description: MOVE THE WAIT AND THE CLAIM BACK INTO THE WRAPPER, BOTH SCRIPTS IN LOCKSTEP. Edit scripts/moe-agent.ps1 and scripts/moe-agent.sh together - same behaviour, same operator-visible strings, same code names - because a one-sided fix fails parity-check and leaves half the fleet broken. Replace the taskless launch for claiming roles with a wrapper-side wait: call wait_for_task through the existing RPC helper with the role's statuses instead of rendering a prompt that asks the CLI to do it. Three outcomes. A task: claim it in the wrapper, populate the same task id, title and pre-flight-ok variables the normal path sets, and fall through to the EXISTING baseline block and the existing launch - no new baseline code and no second landing path, because the point is to rejoin machinery that already works, and that block now also writes the sibling's live-session marker, which a claiming session should have. A routed mention: launch a chat-only session whose prompt says to read and answer the mention and explicitly not to claim or edit; that session legitimately gets no baseline and no marker. A timeout: loop and wait again, reusing the wrapper's existing relaunch loop rather than adding a second one. Leave the governor path alone - a taskless state is normal for that role, it does not claim, and its prompt stays as it is. Preserve the marker comments the regression harness slices on. Error handling: a failed or unreachable wait_for_task must back off and retry rather than falling through to launching an unbound CLI, because that fallback is exactly the hole being closed, and it must not burn the resume budget, which counts attempts at a HELD task rather than idle waiting.
implementationPlan.note:
WAIT AND CLAIM MOVED INTO THE WRAPPER, both scripts in lockstep, same operator strings, same code names.

WHAT LANDED (identical structure in ps1 and sh)
1. Per-iteration state beside the existing pre-flight vars: preflightClaimFailed / preflightWaitFailed / preflightChatOnly / preflightHasUnreadMention (PREFLIGHT_* in sh).
2. MOE_TASKLESS_WAIT_SEC / $moeTasklessWaitSec, default 300, clamped [5,600] - the daemon caps wait_for_task at 600s and moe-proxy already tiers that tool to 11 minutes, so the existing RPC helper carries it with no new plumbing.
3. ROLE_GROUP_TAG hoisted above the claim (it was defined inside the mention-extraction block below) plus a small "is anything ALREADY unread tagging me" probe. This is load-bearing, not decoration: moe.wait_for_task wakes only on NEW MESSAGE_CREATED events, so entering the wait holding an unanswered mention would sit on it for the full timeout.
4. The wait itself, immediately after the claim RPC and before the existing parse, so everything downstream is untouched. It runs only when AutoClaim is on, the role is not governor, no mention is pending, and the claim came back with neither hasNext nor alreadyAssigned.taskId (the resume path keeps ownership of held tasks). Four outcomes: hasNext -> re-issue claim_next_task and fall through to the EXISTING claim parse, get_context, announce, baseline block and launch - no new baseline code, no second landing path, and because the sibling's live-session marker is written inside that same baseline block, a claiming session now picks up baseline AND marker for free; hasChatMessage -> preflightChatOnly, a chat-only launch that legitimately gets neither; timeout -> stays taskless; RPC null -> preflightWaitFailed, back off, do NOT launch. Idle waiting never touches the resume counters, which exist for relaunches at a HELD task.
5. Claim-RPC failure under AutoClaim no longer falls back to the in-agent claim chain - that fallback IS the hole, just triggered by an unreachable daemon instead of an empty board. It sets preflightClaimFailed and backs off. AutoClaim=false keeps the old fallback verbatim: the operator opted out of wrapper claiming, baseline and landing.
6. The taskless prompt gate widened from (claude AND headless AND loopEnabled) to every claiming role under AutoClaim, so no supported path can still render "FIRST action MUST be moe.wait_for_task ... then claim_next_task".
7. ONE launch decision for ALL FOUR CLI types, taken before the dispatch ($moeSkipLaunch / MOE_SKIP_LAUNCH) and emitted as MOE_TASKLESS_NO_LAUNCH reason=idle|wait-failed|claim-failed. It is deliberately NOT gated on loopEnabled: a --no-loop run has already done its waiting in the wrapper. The two per-branch fast paths (grok, claude) were deleted - they were subsumed and their loopEnabled gate now contradicts the rule. This also closes an asymmetry step 1 measured: sh had fast paths only for claude and grok, so codex and gemini seats launched taskless on every poll while ps1's was CLI-agnostic. Governor is excluded everywhere; its prompt is untouched.

ONE EXTRA FIX, MEASURED NECESSARY, NOT SPECULATIVE. scripts/moe-agent.sh invoked python as "$PYTHON_CMD" (quoted) at 7 sites while 57 other sites use $PYTHON_CMD unquoted. find_python returns "py -3" on Windows Git Bash when python3 is absent - this box - so those 7 quoted sites ran a command literally named "py -3" and failed 127 every time. Effect: the routed-mention extraction ALWAYS failed closed, stamped a MOE_MENTION_DELIVERY_FAILED marker with count=1, and that phantom mention forced a CLI launch on every taskless iteration. I found it because it made my own no-launch path unreachable on this box (scenario AA still launched a CLI after the fix). It is 7 characters-per-site, matches the file's own dominant convention, and without it the fix is untestable and mention delivery stays broken on every Windows bash seat. ps1 has no equivalent (it calls node/git directly).

VERIFIED SO FAR
- `bash -n scripts/moe-agent.sh` clean; PowerShell AST ParseFile on moe-agent.ps1 reports PARSE OK.
- `node --test scripts/tests/taskless-handoff.test.mjs`: tests 39, pass 39, fail 0 (was 21/18 before this step).
- `MOE_POSTFLIGHT_TIMEOUT_SEC=180 bash scripts/tests/postflight.sh`: PASS, "commit-scope scenarios run: 28", exit 0 - including the 26 pre-existing scenarios and the recovery-race sibling's M2.
- Standalone end-to-end reproduction against the real wrapper and the harness's own fake proxy: with no claimable task the wrapper prints the wait line and then MOE_TASKLESS_NO_LAUNCH reason=idle with NO CLI spawned; with the wait woken by a chat message the chat-only session launches, and the adoption probe then fires (step 4).
- postflight.ps1 running sequentially; result recorded in step 5.

Shared checkout: peer/pre-existing dirty paths untouched, unstaged, unreverted.

implementationPlan.description: ADD THE ADOPTION BOUNDARY AS A LOUD REFUSAL, BOTH SCRIPTS. The wrapper-side wait closes the supported paths, but a chat-only or governor session could still end up holding a task - an agent ignoring its prompt, or a future launch path nobody has written - and today that ends in silence. In the post-flight of a session that launched WITHOUT a task, look up whether the worker now holds one. If not, behave exactly as today. If it does and the tree is clean, say so and exit quietly. If it does and the tree is dirty, refuse to land, emit a named code in the existing MOE_COMMIT_REFUSED_ family so parity-check enforces it across both wrappers automatically, print an operator line naming the task and the absence of a pre-edit baseline, and post one governors chat line. Do NOT invent a baseline and do NOT stage the tree - both are forbidden by the task rails, and with no baseline the wrapper genuinely cannot separate this session's bytes from a peer's work in progress or from dirt that predated it. Be honest about the consequence in the operator line and in the completion summary: those bytes stay in the working tree unlanded, and because the next session of that task snapshots them as pre-existing, a human must deal with them. That residual is exactly why the wrapper-side wait is the real fix and this guard is only the alarm. Keep both wrappers byte-parallel in wording.
implementationPlan.note:
ADOPTION BOUNDARY LANDED IN BOTH WRAPPERS, as an alarm, not a recovery.

Placement: the post-flight's existing `AutoClaim AND preflightTaskId` landing block gets an `elif` sibling - a session that launched WITHOUT a task, where a CLI actually ran (MOE_SKIP_LAUNCH=false, so a suppressed launch costs nothing), role != governor.

Probe: `moe.get_context` with ONLY a workerId. getContext.ts (packages/moe-daemon/src/tools/getContext.ts:94-104) falls back to the caller's worker.currentTaskId when no taskId is given, and the call has no side effects. `claim_next_task` is deliberately NOT used - it would CLAIM a task rather than report one. `list_workers` was my first choice and is wrong: its inputSchema is additionalProperties:false and moe-proxy injects MOE_WORKER_ID into every tools/call that omits workerId, so the daemon would reject the probe outright. Verified in packages/moe-proxy/src/utils.ts:166-187 (only get_activity_log is exempt).

Three outcomes, identical wording in both wrappers:
- Worker holds nothing -> behaves exactly as before (nothing printed, nothing done).
- Holds a task, tree clean -> one quiet `[adoption]` line, exit.
- Holds a task, tree dirty -> refuse. `MOE_COMMIT_REFUSED_ADOPTED_NO_BASELINE task=<id> worker=<id> dirty=<n>` plus a full operator sentence, and one @governors line into #general. The code sits in the MOE_COMMIT_REFUSED_ family, so parity-check.sh/.ps1 enforce its presence in BOTH wrappers with no harness edit.

No baseline is invented and nothing is staged - both forbidden by the task rails, and genuinely impossible to do safely: with no pre-edit snapshot the wrapper cannot separate this session's bytes from a live peer's work in progress or from dirt that predated the session. Dirtiness is read with the same `status --porcelain=v1 -z --untracked-files=all --no-renames` invocation the rest of the landing machinery uses.

THE RESIDUAL, stated plainly in the operator line, in the chat line and again here: those bytes stay in the working tree UNLANDED, and because the next session of that task snapshots them as pre-existing, only a human can land or discard them. That is why the wrapper-side wait in step 3 is the real fix and this guard is only the alarm for a path nobody has written.

VERIFIED BEHAVIOURALLY, not by reading:
- Standalone run against the real scripts/moe-agent.sh and the postflight harness's own fake proxy, wait woken by a chat message and the worker holding task-adopted: `MOE_COMMIT_REFUSED_ADOPTED_NO_BASELINE task=task-adopted worker=worker-repro dirty=4 - ...` printed, no commit made.
- `MOE_POSTFLIGHT_TIMEOUT_SEC=180 bash scripts/tests/postflight.sh` PASS, 28 scenarios, exit 0. Scenario AB asserts the named code, that HEAD did NOT move, that the session's own file is still untracked, that a PEER's modified file is still ` M` and untouched, and that the refusal actually reached the #general message store rather than only stdout (asserting the code alone would have been green on a print-only implementation).
- postflight.ps1 twin running sequentially; its result is recorded in step 5.

implementationPlan.description: RUN EVERY GATE, THEN A REAL CANARY. (b) `bash scripts/tests/parity-check.sh` and its PowerShell twin must both pass, which is what proves the wrappers stayed in lockstep including the new refusal code. (c) `bash scripts/tests/postflight.sh` and `scripts/tests/postflight.ps1`, run SEQUENTIALLY on an otherwise quiet box with MOE_POSTFLIGHT_TIMEOUT_SEC=180 - the default sixty seconds flakes while the fleet runs its own suites and the heartbeat-sidecar check fails first. Both harnesses gained cases from the recovery-race sibling, so read a failure there as possibly ITS case rather than assuming yours. Never pipe a harness through grep with pipefail set, which turns a real failure into a silent exit code. (d) The canary the Definition of Done requires: launch one real wrapper seat against a board state with no claimable task for that role, let it wait, let a task appear, and confirm from evidence rather than console - a per-task baseline exists under the git directory BEFORE any edit, the session lands a task-scoped commit, and moe.get_context for that task shows the commit recorded with path-specific attribution. Capture the task id, the baseline path and the sha. If a canary is impossible in the current environment, say so plainly rather than reporting an untested fix as verified. (e) Record every command, exit code and count for the verification argument of complete_task.

The first canary run FAILED with "moe.wait_for_task did not answer", and a direct probe against the real daemon returned {"code":-32000,"message":"Proxy shutting down before response received"}. implementationPlan.note:
ADVERSARIAL REVIEW. Read the diff as an attacker; three real findings, all fixed before completing.

FIXED DURING THIS STEP
1. The single launch decision sat immediately BEFORE `$script:CliLaunchedAt = Get-Date`, which is the END boundary of the psBody slice taskless-handoff.test.mjs renders. That pulled live launch logic into the prompt fixture (it passed, but only by accident of which variables the fixture happens to define). Moved after the marker so the slice stays prompt-only. All four marker comments verified present and unchanged afterwards.
2. The adoption boundary excluded the governor. Wrong: a governor holding a task is precisely the unanticipated path the alarm exists for, and the probe costs one side-effect-free RPC at session end. Exclusion removed in both wrappers.
3. My first adoption probe was going to be `moe.list_workers`. It cannot work: the tool's inputSchema is `additionalProperties:false` and moe-proxy injects `workerId` into every tools/call that omits it (packages/moe-proxy/src/utils.ts:166-187 exempts only get_activity_log), so the daemon would reject the call. Replaced with `get_context {workerId}`, whose documented fallback resolves the caller's held task.

EVERY REMAINING LAUNCH PATH, WALKED
- AutoClaim + claiming role + no task + no mention -> no launch (MOE_TASKLESS_NO_LAUNCH reason=idle).
- Claim RPC null -> reason=claim-failed, no launch, outer loop backs off. Closes H4.
- Single-shot (-NoLoop) -> bounded in-wrapper re-claim, then no launch. Closes H1.
- Mention pending -> chat-only session, all CLI types, interactive included. Closes H2/H3. That session CAN still physically edit; nothing in a wrapper can stop a rogue agent, which is exactly why the adoption alarm exists.
- Resume (alreadyAssigned.taskId) -> wait is SKIPPED, normal bound path, untouched.
- BLOCKED hold and resume-cap-exhausted -> alreadyAssigned present so the wait is skipped, then no launch; no relaunch and no resume attempt burned, preserving the existing BLOCKED contract.
- Governor -> launches as before with the governance prompt; never claims.
- AutoClaim=false -> byte-identical old behaviour (no wrapper claim, no baseline, no landing: the operator owns it).

RESUME BUDGET: the bounded wait only runs when NO task is held and breaks the moment one appears, and `$script:ResumeAttempts` / RESUME_ATTEMPTS are still incremented exactly once per iteration in the untouched parse block. Idle waiting costs nothing from a budget that exists for relaunches at a HELD task.

NO IDLE-BASED AUTO-RELEASE SMUGGLED IN: nothing in the diff releases, unassigns or marks a worker dead. The bounded wait's `claim_next_task` calls touch the worker, so a waiting seat looks MORE alive, not less.

WRAPPER STILL THE ONLY GIT ACTOR, ATTRIBUTION UNRELAXED: `git diff -- scripts/ | grep '^+'` finds no `git add -A`, no `git add -u`, no bare `git commit` in either wrapper (the two added `git commit` lines are inside the test harnesses building disposable fixture repos), and no forbidden pattern from the project rails. No baseline is created anywhere outside the existing pre-flight block; the adoption path deliberately creates none. Peer path sets unchanged; scenario AB asserts a peer's dirty file is still ` M` after the refusal.

- ps1 parses `git status --porcelain -z` by joining native output and splitting on NUL. If PowerShell mangles the NULs the count collapses toward 1 instead of 0, i.e. it errs toward RAISING the alarm, never toward silence. Scenario AB passes in the ps1 harness, so the count is nonzero there.

planningNotes.approachesConsidered: Detecting the in-CLI claim after the fact and taking a baseline then - rejected: by the time the wrapper notices, edits have happened, so the snapshot would record this session's own work as pre-existing, which is worse than no baseline. Hand-creating a baseline for an adopted task, or staging the whole tree when a taskless session ends dirty - both rejected by task rails; the latter would sweep up peer work in progress and dirt that predated the session. Leaving the idle CLI to claim while teaching post-flight to land whatever it finds - rejected for the same attribution reason. That leaves the option the card names first and which is structurally correct: keep the waiting and claiming in the wrapper so a session that can edit code is only ever launched with a task already bound, and let the existing baseline and landing machinery run untouched. The routed-mention case is the one legitimate taskless launch, so it gets a chat-only session told not to claim or edit, and the adoption guard stays as a loud alarm for any path nobody anticipated.

This row carried an intact six-step plan and zero completed steps; it was moved back to BACKLOG and re-promoted, and since PLANNING cannot transition straight to WORKING, resubmitting the approved shape is the only legal route back. The steps are unchanged in substance; step 1 is refreshed for one thing that happened in between. The defect itself is a three-site asymmetry rather than a subtle race: the taskless prompt instructs the CLI to wait, claim and fetch context itself, while both the baseline block and the post-flight landing are gated on a task id that pre-flight never set. So the session most likely to start editing from a cold start is exactly the one with no snapshot of what was already dirty and no landing at the end, and it fails with no error at all - just nothing. What changed: task-e5a45262, the QA recovery race, has LANDED in these same two wrappers and both postflight harnesses. It writes a live-session marker in the same pre-flight block that takes the baseline and gates recovery on probing that marker's process. That makes this fix cleaner rather than harder - once the wrapper claims before launching, a claiming session passes through that block and picks up both the baseline and the marker with no new code here, while a chat-only session correctly gets neither because it holds no task. Every line number in the earlier version of this plan is now suspect, which is why step 1 re-measures.
